messages.author: 12f269733c6eb9a2
messages.subject: Re: replicate lines and one-sided lines
parts:
Laurent:

I'm sure several people on this list will want to tell you about the
'challenges' you face by detecting animals from a vehicle. It seems
unlikely that you can drive the vehicle randomly through the vineyard
(at least you cannot do this with the vineyard owner's permission).
Without that random component, you face the issue that the hares you
wish to study are not distributed in the vineyard at uniform distances
from where you are driving (tracks of some sort). This will cause you
many problems with regard to the interpretation of the distribution of
detection distances. This was most recently discussed on this list in a
message fro 6 November by Len Thomas (consult the Distance list archives
to find this message). In that message, Len sends interested readers to
an advanced treatment of this topic within a dissertation by Tiago
Marques found at

http://hdl.handle.net/10023/391

If/when you resolve those issues, you will then be able to address the question of specifying a multiplier for
one-sided transects (found in Chapter 8 of the Users Guide, under the heading 'Multipliers in CDS analysis').
And regarding repeat visits over a transect, you can multiply the length of the transect by the number of
times it is travelled and use that as the amount of effort associated with that transect.


Laurent TATIN Laurent Tatin Mas petit Rebattu Moules F-13280

messages.author: 6e15de0134e98c08
messages.subject: Re: replicate lines and one-sided lines
parts:
Hi Laurent, list,

I add to Eric's message that 1 sided transects are usually discouraged,
being potentially problematic unless there is a very clear definition of
what is the transect line. Otherwise there is a tendency to record
animals "just on the other side" that the driver (using your wording)
records as "on the line". This leads to too many detections at 0 and a
corresponding overestimation of density. But as Eric said, this will
only be an issue to worry about once you have dealt with the non-uniform
distribution of distances which you seem to have to deal with at present.

It was not clear from your description if the lines are placed along
roads, or trails, or any other linear feature that the hares might
respond to. Feel free to contact me off the line if you want to explain
this further.

All the best,

Tiago
